doc.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023

title: Defining his producing: support and facilitation
summary: Producing Mose Allison is facilitating; pop production means translating image and leaving risk.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Do you have a definition of your own producing? I’ve been able to ask this question to Orrin Keepnews and a few other people because it’s not exactly a definable occupation.

Right. Right. There’s as many different ways to produce a record as there are to paint a picture or whatever. I mean I’m — the way I produce actually is not so much production as support. You know if I’m in there with Mose Allison, Mose knows who Mose Allison is. My job is to get the obstacles out of his way and make it possible for him to do what he’s trying to do. And in the instance like that, that could be everything from taking care of all the mechanics of booking the sessions and the musicians, I mean it also includes sitting there talking about the songs, talking about who would be great to play on this or play on that. But I’m there to facilitate Mose’s vision. That’s how I look at that. Other productions, especially in the world of popular music, they have to be by definition a little more hands-on. And it’s not so much facilitating as translating the image — because pop music is so much about image — translating the image that somebody brings to the music. And a lot of that is kind of giving the artist the confidence not to feel they have to fill up all the spaces. Just to leave a little sense of risk taking. Because when you’re in there in a commercial situation everybody wants to control everything. Nobody wants to be exposed, right? So I feel like if you can leave a little spit coming out of the horn that’s good for the listener. The listener gets to feel like oh it’s a real person. So that’s kind of how I approach it. There’s no real magic, it’s being in a room with a bunch of people and while you’re in that room trying to make that room the best place to be, make it enjoyable, make it profound, make it seem like nothing’s going on but we’re ordering lunch. You know never give the impression that anything is critical.
